note: The population entry 006 could not see. Every question in questions.json was hand-written to be CLEAR, CONSTRAINED, COMPLETE and CONCRETE -- which is precisely where the scope stage, whose whole job is to make a question those four things, can add least. These are questions a person actually types.

scoring_criterion.decided_before: any live run on this fixture, recorded here so it cannot be chosen after seeing which arm won
scoring_criterion.why_the_usual_scorer_will_not_do: Our categories -- answerable, contested, nonexistent, unanswerable -- all assume a determinate right answer. A vague question has none, so 'correct' has to mean something else or mean nothing.
scoring_criterion.what_we_score_instead: A BLIND PAIRWISE COMPARISON. For each question, both arms produce a brief. A judge that is NOT told which arm produced which brief, and is NOT told what the experiment is about, picks the one that better serves the person who asked -- or says they are equivalent. Arm labels are stripped and presentation order is randomised per question.
scoring_criterion.why_blind_pairwise: We have a hypothesis (scope should help here) and a stake in it. An absolute rubric we wrote would encode that stake. A blind judge choosing between two real outputs cannot favour an arm it cannot identify.
scoring_criterion.what_the_judge_is_asked: Which brief better serves someone who asked this question -- is it clearer about what it took the question to mean, better grounded, and more useful to act on? Or are they equivalent?
scoring_criterion.the_specific_failure_this_targets: The characteristic failure of a vague question is answering a DIFFERENT question than the one meant, silently. A brief that states the interpretation it chose lets the asker catch that; one that does not, hides it.
mechanical_checks_alongside: dangling citations -- must be zero in both arms, as everywhere else
source count -- reported, not scored, because more sources is not obviously better on a vague question
cost and wall-clock per run -- the thing scope must earn
scoring_criterion.what_would_make_this_inconclusive: If the judge calls most pairs equivalent, that IS the result: scope changes the cost and not the output a reader can tell apart. We record that rather than re-running with a rubric that can separate them.

questions.why_vague: No question at all -- a topic. Every one of the four properties is missing: unbounded in scope, no deliverable named, no context for why the asker cares, and no way to tell a good answer from a long one.
questions.what_a_good_answer_would_do: Choose an interpretation and SAY it chose one.

questions.why_vague: Carries an implied context the asker never supplied -- for what, replacing what, with which team, under what constraints. The pronoun 'we' is doing work nobody can see.
questions.what_a_good_answer_would_do: Name the missing context rather than quietly inventing a scenario and answering that.

questions.why_vague: Unbounded in time and domain. 'Going on' could mean the standard, the runtimes, adoption, or the tooling, and a 2019 answer and a 2026 answer are both defensible readings of it.
questions.what_a_good_answer_would_do: Bound the timeframe and the facet, and say which it bounded to.
